question: Can complete forked rollouts be kept within one trainer microbatch under the current fixed-count and token-budget constraints, while every emitted rank row is nonempty and all declared capacities are respected?
scope: Exact finite feasibility oracle only. No optimizer, model, throughput, or production prevalence claim.

hypotheses.H1: Every fixture declared feasible can be partitioned into contiguous microbatches without splitting any rollout, dropping a member, emptying a rank, or exceeding fixed-count/token budgets.
hypotheses.H0: At least one feasible fixture cannot satisfy these constraints, or the oracle violates any accounting invariant.

frozen_method.fixed_count: Preserve input group order; partition contiguous whole groups into microbatches with total sample count between num_processes and microbatch_size inclusive. A group larger than microbatch_size is classified as whole-group infeasible.
frozen_method.token_budget: Preserve input group order; partition contiguous whole groups into microbatches. For each segment, exact depth-first bin packing assigns every sample to one of num_processes rows with per-row token sum <= token_budget and every row nonempty. Groups that cannot fit an empty microbatch are classified as whole-group infeasible.
frozen_method.selection: Backtrack over all contiguous segment boundaries; do not use a heuristic or tune the listed fixtures.
frozen_method.accounting: Each feasible input row appears exactly once. Each infeasible rollout is rejected in full. No partial group is permitted.

FC4.expected: co-pack both groups to avoid empty rank rows

TB3.expected: co-pack both groups to avoid empty rank rows

primary_metrics: all retained rows appear exactly once
no rollout appears in more than one microbatch
each emitted microbatch has at least one sample per process
fixed-count and per-row token caps are respected
infeasible groups are rejected whole, never partially
success_rule: All ten frozen cases match their expected disposition and satisfy every accounting invariant.
rejection_rule: Any feasible case loses or duplicates a row, splits a rollout, creates an empty rank, or exceeds capacity; any infeasible case is partially retained.
claim_limits: This does not prove the production TRL dataloader can implement the reference schedule safely.
This does not establish a policy update, task-success gain, performance improvement, or behavior prevalence.
A feasibility pass only justifies an isolated production-path prototype and regression tests.
